close_reason: Added a PLAN.md §'Classifier-attribute strings are bare Option<String> / String' section explaining the workspace 'externally-owned-schema classifier strings' exclusion for these 9 fields, with redirect to the workspace AGENTS.md policy and the README §Gotchas note. The bead's defensive intent — a future contributor proposing 'type these properly' as an enum should be redirected to existing policy, not have the policy rediscovered — is now visible in all three places (workspace AGENTS.md, crate PLAN.md, crate README). No code change. Tests pass.
description: lib.rs types NameComponent.kind:150, Title.kind:334, Calendar.kind:515, Anniversary.kind:1009, PersonalInfo.kind:1098, Directory.kind:744, Link.kind:799, Media.kind:847, AddressComponent.kind:667 as Option<String> or String — NOT as #[non_exhaustive] enum { Variant, …, Other(String) }. This follows the workspace AGENTS.md 'externally-owned-schema classifier strings' exclusion (decided 2026-05-12). The rationale documented there: RFC 9553 enumerates these values as if authoritative, but real-world JSContact emitters (Outlook, Google, Apple, vCard converters, localized clients) routinely send values outside the spec enumeration, so a typed enum would do no real programmatic dispatch and pay a maintenance cost for every spec revision. A future contributor unfamiliar with the workspace policy will see the bare String and propose 'typing these properly' as an enum — defend the current shape, point them at workspace AGENTS.md, and link the README §Gotchas note at :99-107 that already explains the choice.
title: Classifier-attribute strings typed as Option<String>, not enum-with-Other
